perspective:
Arthur’s accessible information:

- He knows he and Teresa are professional colleagues who have worked together on community-service projects.
- During the current project, he observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He feels concerned and decides to offer help.
- He says: “Hey Teresa, I noticed you've been working really hard and seem a bit overwhelmed. Is there anything I can help you with?”
- He hears Teresa say she thinks she can manage but there is a lot to do. He insists on helping; she accepts help organizing medical supplies. They start.
- He believes Teresa is hesitant to accept help because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy and reassures her that accepting help does not mean she is not capable.
- He hears Teresa say she wants to show she can do it by herself, appreciates his point, and admits she sometimes needs reminding. He tells her teamwork is about getting the job done and that he supports her.
- He believes Teresa is still struggling and feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results. He tells her he can see things are still tough and that she is doing a great job.
- He hears Teresa say it has been a busy day and she feels like she is falling behind. He suggests working together instead of just helping her. She agrees.
- He feels hopeful about the collaborative approach. He hears Teresa say it already feels less overwhelming. They agree he will handle inventory, she will manage patient records, and they will check in regularly.
- Afterward, he believes their collaboration paid off and strengthened their professional relationship. He feels satisfied.
- He hears Teresa agree it was a great experience and that they are more efficient as a team. He proposes continuing the collaborative approach in future projects; she agrees. He looks forward to their next project together.

He does not have access to Teresa’s unspoken private thoughts or any narrator-only information beyond what he observed, heard, said, did, or already knew from their professional relationship.
